articles.title: Gary Marcus: ‘Just Say No to Anthropic’s IPO’
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、Startup & business
articles.summary: Gary Marcus: When a business needs exponentially increasing amounts of capital to make modest increases in quality in an intensely competitive market and still owes far more money than it has ever made, there is a serious problem. I continue to believe that there is no moat in AI models. None. But the entire premise of Anthropic’s IPO is that they have an enormous gulf of a moat. I would not be shocked to see Anthropic go out of business. Nor would I be shocked if the IPO fails.

articles.title: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、Startup & business
articles.summary: OpenAI has not yet said what its plans are for the future of travel. But Sonder founder Francis Davidson is a well-known figure in the travel industry.
articles.full_text:
OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson.

Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire.

Davidson’s announcement focused largely on how he built his AI travel agent Odessia by directing teams of AI agents.

The year-old Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent around five months ago.

Davidson says that it had helped early adopters plan millions of dollars’ worth of travel, but the tool has already been shut down.

An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the hire to TechCrunch. “We’re thrilled to welcome Francis to OpenAI.

Francis is a proven founder who has built multiple businesses to help people travel, and we’re excited he’s chosen to build with us.” However the AI lab has not announced new travel-specific products or plans.

It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners.

Travel is also one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with.

And, back in July 2025, when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT agent , it mentioned travel as one of its potential uses.

OpenAI’s spokesperson didn’t have more to share on its plans for travel-related products, except to say that travel is one of the areas that chatbot users frequently ask about. “1.2 billion people turn to ChatGPT each week for help with everyday tasks — from understanding their health, figuring out what to make for dinner, building a budget, and even planning a trip.

We see a real opportunity to make these experiences even more useful,” the spokesperson said.

Acquiring Odessia is interesting for another reason.

Davidson is well known in the travel industry after he founded a travel startup called Sonder as a college student in 2014.

It was sort of like Airbnb, but it focused on short-term leasing of upscale apartments in major cities worldwide.

The pandemic badly hurt it, and as it climbed out of that rut, it went public via a SPAC but didn’t raise as much money as it needed, Davidson later said in a post announcing his resignation as CEO in June 2025.

When a key partnership with Marriott fell through , the company went into bankruptcy and wound down.

The bankruptcy trustee sold Sonder’s name, trademarks, and website domain in 2026 to TravelAI, and that website operates as a curated guide to the kind of travel rental properties that Sonder was once known for.

Prior to its downfall, Davidson had built Sonder into a unicorn with $143 million in revenues.

While Sonder was not, ultimately, a success story, Davidson is the kind of battle-scarred founder that Silicon Valley often values.

So we’ll have to wait and see what OpenAI has in store now with travel, now that he’s joined the company.

Note: This story was updated with OpenAI’s comments.

articles.title: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、Startup & business
articles.summary: Each of the seven co-founders plans to sell exactly the same number of shares in the IPO, which would bring each of them about $250 million in cash at the midpoint of the price range while leaving the group in control of the company.
articles.full_text:
As Anthropic barrels toward an enormous IPO that could value it at $1.4 trillion, the company has disclosed a tidbit in its new S-1 filing about how many shares each of its seven co-founders plan to sell.

Each will sell 3,378,378 shares.

Anthropic has floated an unusually broad initial price range of $70 to $78 a share.

At the midrange of $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million.

At the low end, $70, each would have to settle for pocketing just over $236 million in cash; at the high end, $78, each would take in just under $264 million.

However, in an IPO as eagerly anticipated as this one, companies can often price shares above the initial range.

The S-1 is already hinting at high demand.

Board member Reed Hastings has indicated he wants to buy $300 million worth of shares through his donor-advised fund.

Board member Christopher Liddell also wants to buy $3 million worth of shares.

The seven co-founders are Dario Amodei, CEO; Daniela Amodei, president and chair of the board; Tom Brown, chief compute officer; Jack Clark, head of public benefit; Jared Kaplan, chief science officer (pictured above); Sam McCandlish, chief architect; and Christopher Olah, interpretability research lead.

After the sale, each of them will own about 3.2% of the total outstanding Class A shares, the S-1 says, or roughly 22% collectively.

That’s not their share of the company overall.

Class A is just one of Anthropic’s share classes, and other holders, including Amazon and Google, hold nonvoting Class N shares, so the founders’ stake in the company’s total equity will be considerably smaller.

Even still, they, as a group, remain in control of the company.

Each will also receive one share of Class F stock, which carries supervoting rights.

Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of the votes, but no single founder will hold significantly more shares or votes than the others.

As is now industry lore, the seven left OpenAI to start Anthropic in 2021 after disagreements with OpenAI’s leadership over how AI should be built.

Siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, who held senior research and policy roles at OpenAI, were joined by five fellow OpenAI colleagues in forming a company that has said, very publicly and from the start, that it’s more focused on AI safety than its rivals, including the founders’ former employer.

articles.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、AI agent & application
articles.summary: Users can now interact with Meta’s AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation on their Apple Watch.
articles.full_text:
Meta is bringing its Muse AI agent to the Apple Watch and Android’s Wear OS, the company announced on Monday.

With the launch, users can now interact with Meta’s AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation directly on their smartwatch.

The smartwatch launch comes just a month after Meta introduced a dedicated iPad app for Muse.

First launched on the App Store in September, the AI assistant’s expansion across Apple devices signals Meta’s growing ambitions for its consumer AI product and its focus on making Muse a central part of its ecosystem.

Muse is now one of dozens of consumer-facing AI agents competing for users’ attention.

Like many of its competitors, it allows users to connect their accounts to manage email, meetings, bills, and more, while also handling tasks such as booking reservations, ordering groceries, setting goals, and making purchases.

Users can also personalize their Muse avatar to their liking and change it into something that resembles a person, an animal, or another type of character.

Despite being a relatively new product, Meta has wasted little time introducing new capabilities to Muse.

A few days ago, Meta launched Spaces , a new way to communicate and collaborate with Muse.

Spaces function as dedicated conversations around specific topics, which Meta describes as “custom experiences” as they’re mini apps that are built on the fly.

They appear in the sidebar of the Muse interface and bring up a focused conversation where the AI agent works toward a particular goal on the user’s behalf.

Last week, Meta rolled out the ability for users in the U.S. to video chat with their Muse AI avatar.

Meta said Muse will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that reflect the tone and context of the conversation as it speaks.

It’s worth noting that Muse doesn’t actually see users, but can hear them and respond in real time.

Shortly after its launch, Muse became one of just 12 mobile apps to have surpassed 10 million U.S. downloads within their first 40 days in the App Store.

Only 11 other apps have achieved this milestone, with Meta’s Threads being the most recent in July 2023.

Its IPO price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share, which would put its valuation as high as $1.4 trillion, according to the The New York Times. The Wall Street Journal […]
articles.full_text:
AI Business News Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion IPO Anthropic’s public offering is expected to make it one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies as soon as next week.

Anthropic’s public offering is expected to make it one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies as soon as next week. by Stevie Bonifield Nov 10, 2026, 2:06 PM UTC Link Share Gift Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge Stevie Bonifield is a news writer covering all things consumer tech.

Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Anthropic confirmed on Tuesday that its IPO could be one of the biggest ever, even while falling short of previous expectations.

Its IPO price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share, which would put its valuation as high as $1.4 trillion, according to the The New York Times .

The Wall Street Journal reports that according to its sources, Anthropic is “aiming for its shares to start trading Thursday or Friday next week.” As Reuters notes, the Anthropic IPO was previously expected to be valued at as much as $2 trillion.

As of last week, Anthropic’s rival OpenAI was valued at $1.25 trillion .

Those lower expectations follow months of debate around AI safety , and what that means, while midterm election results showed souring public opinion toward AI companies and data center projects they’re heavily investing in.

And that doesn’t even include this past weekend’s revelations about an alleged Chinese spy’s involvement with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang .

According to Anthropic: The initial public offering price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share.

Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.” Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.
